title: Master Services Agreement

origin.title: Master Services Agreement with Power DMS by NEOGOV, with Exhibit A order form (attachment to the Commissioners Court agenda of February 11, 2025)
origin.clearance_note: A county contract published by Williamson County, Texas as an attachment to its Commissioners Court agenda of February 11, 2025, linked from the public agenda at https://public.destinyhosted.com/94526/agenda/agenda.cfm?seq=1872. Downloaded by script. Published as the county filed it, by the document owner's explicit decision: nothing was replaced. The county had already blacked out the order form's account and order numbers, and no text sits under those boxes. The parties are a county and a software company. The vendor's signer appears in a professional capacity on pages 5 and 7, with two DocuSign signatures and a legal-review initials stamp; the county's signature blocks are blank. Contact details on the order form are a county department's accounts-payable mailbox and office phone. The PDF carried no metadata.

notes: The request named no feature page or fields; its notes suggested page 6, the Exhibit A order form, with the customer, the Net 60 payment term, a subscription line item with dates and quantity, and the prorated total, as suggestions only. Page 6 ships. The customer grounds OFF (the name wraps across two lines in its cell) and every line item's start date grounds OFF (10/1/2024 is printed without zero padding and is extracted as an ISO date), so neither is featured. The overlay reads as one purchase: Net 60 terms, the PowerPolicy Professional Subscription for 89 users, prorated through 11/30/2024, inside the $1,260.69 prorated table. No person is featured. The signer's name and signatures are left as published at the document owner's decision. Table grounding was sensitive to the schema: rewording the description of one unrelated field (county.name, on page 1) made two further extractions ground every cell of the prorated table to its heading, 'Prorated to Shift Dates'; restoring the original wording restored cell-level grounding, and that run is the one committed. The cost is that county.name comes back as 'Williamson' rather than 'Williamson County, Texas'.
